answer: On an island trading network, agents booking cargo through the inlet must each lock 100 credits in escrow until delivery is verified, even for a small shipment of umber pigment. The same credits cannot back two active identities. An attacker can invent names freely, but operating 1,000 fake agents requires tying up 100,000 credits for the full settlement period, making each additional active identity consume scarce capital and forgo its use elsewhere.
